criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A shard.rs unit test calls the real selection with a fixture timings map for n=6 and asserts that the largest per-shard duration total is at most 1.25 times the mean, and that each fixture unit appears in exactly one shard.
criteria.evidence: `timed_shards_are_balanced_and_partition_the_units` passed. It calls the real `select` for k in 0..6 over the 40-unit `many_units` fixture. It asserts the union has the same length as the units and sorts equal to them, so each unit appears exactly once, and it asserts largest <= 1.25 * mean. Working it out by hand, the old index-modulo rule would fail this test: shard 0 would hold 851s against a mean of 540s, and 851 is more than the 675s bound. So the test depends on the new behavior.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A shard.rs unit test includes a unit absent from the fixture timings and asserts that it is assigned to exactly one shard, with every unit still covered.
criteria.evidence: `a_unit_with_no_timing_is_still_assigned_exactly_once` passed. It adds `new-pkg --test brand_new`, which has no timing. It asserts exactly one shard holds that unit and that the flattened shards equal the full unit list.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`. The existing partition tests pass, including `shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target`, using the real checked-in xtask/shard-timings.txt.
criteria.evidence: 20 passed, 0 failed. This includes shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target, test_shard_6_is_disjoint_and_equals_the_workspace_target_set and the new checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit. These tests run the built `xtask test-shard`, which loads the real xtask/shard-timings.txt through load_timings.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace`. All pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for 197bdcaf from CI run 41409510508: fmt, clippy and test all succeeded.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A shard.rs unit test shows a malformed timings line (missing field or non-numeric seconds) returns an error that names the line.
criteria.evidence: `a_malformed_timings_line_is_an_error_naming_the_line` passed. It covers a missing duration, non-numeric seconds, a negative value, NaN, a missing selector, a single token and a duplicate line. Each error must contain 'shard-timings.txt line', and the error for `# ok\nxtask --lib x` must contain 'line 2'.

criteria.criterion: xtask/src/shard.rs sorts timed units by descending duration and places each on the currently least-loaded shard. Untimed units use the existing sorted index-modulo split. A new xtask subcommand that rewrites xtask/shard-timings.txt from a local run is wired in xtask/src/main.rs and listed in the usage text.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, `assign` sorts timed units with timings[b].total_cmp(timings[a]) (descending, ties broken by unit order) and places each on min_by(load) (ties to the lowest shard). Untimed units are sorted and placed by i % n. main.rs dispatches `shard-timings` to shard::timings_command. The usage output, which I ran, lists `cargo run -p xtask -- shard-timings` with a description.

criteria.criterion: xtask/shard-timings.txt exists and has a line for every current workspace test unit that `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard 0 1 --dry-run` lists, so the real shards are balanced rather than all falling back.
criteria.evidence: The dry run lists 58 units. The file has 58 data lines (63 lines minus 5 header lines), and they match the dry-run list entry for entry. checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit asserts the timed set equals the metadata oracle, and it passed.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing timing-balanced sharding, the timings file and the update command.
criteria.evidence: The new entry under Changed describes longest-first balancing onto the least-loaded shard, xtask/shard-timings.txt and its line format, the fallback for untimed units, and `cargo run -p xtask -- shard-timings`.

findings.summary: The checked-in timings are estimates, not measurements, so real CI balance is unproven until someone refreshes the file.
findings.evidence: The header says 'ESTIMATES: these values are rough guesses scaled to the totals of GitHub run 41221582236'. The reading allows clearly labeled estimates, so this does not violate a criterion. The CHANGELOG reason cites run 41221582236 shard times; that run is not in the snapshot, so I could not check those numbers.

findings.summary: `shard-timings` times each unit with `cargo test -p <pkg>` after a `--workspace --no-run` build. Building per package can resolve dependency features differently and trigger a rebuild, which would inflate the first unit timed in a package.
findings.evidence: The command runs `cargo test --locked --workspace --no-run` and then `cargo test --locked -p <pkg> <selector>` per unit, and records wall time including any build. This is reasoned from the code, not observed: I did not run the command because it runs the whole suite.

findings.summary: The ci_shards coverage test parses the timings file in its own simpler way instead of matching parse_timings.
findings.evidence: It uses `starts_with('#')` without trimming and `rsplit_once(' ')`, while parse_timings trims lines and splits on any whitespace. Both read the current file the same way.

summary: The change meets all eight criteria and stays within the five expected files. `xtask test-shard` now places units with a recorded time longest first, each on the least-loaded shard; units with no time keep the old sorted index-modulo split. A new `shard-timings` command rewrites xtask/shard-timings.txt and is listed in the usage text. The xtask shard unit tests (13 passed) and ci_shards (20 passed) ran here; fmt, clippy and the full test suite are Athena's recorded CI results. The balance test fails under the old rule, by my hand calculation: its biggest shard would be 851s against a 675s bound. The checked-in file covers all 58 units the dry run lists. The minor issue: the file's values are labeled estimates, not measurements, so real CI balance is unproven until someone runs `cargo run -p xtask -- shard-timings` and commits the result.
